steps.tx: Classic distal **renal tubular acidosis**, designated as **Type 1 RTA**, arises from impaired distal alpha-intercalated cell proton secretion caused by mutations in the apical **H+-ATPase** pump or basolateral chloride-bicarbonate exchanger **AE1**. Patients exhibit a hyperchloremic normal anion gap metabolic acidosis and an inability to acidify urine below pH **5.5** despite systemic acidemia.
steps.say: Classic distal renal tubular acidosis, designated as Type 1 RTA, arises from impaired distal alpha-intercalated cell proton secretion caused by mutations in the apical H+-ATPase pump or basolateral chloride-bicarbonate exchanger AE1. Affected patients have a hyperchloremic normal anion gap metabolic acidosis and an inability to acidify urine below pH 5 point 5 despite systemic acidemia.

vis.caption: Alpha-intercalated cell transport defects in distal Type 1 RTA. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Type 1 RTA** characteristically causes recurrent calcium nephrolithiasis and extensive medullary **nephrocalcinosis** throughout both kidneys. This devastating structural complication results directly from persistent alkaline urine pH driving calcium phosphate precipitation, excessive hypercalciuria from skeletal acid buffering, and severe **hypocitraturia** secondary to enhanced proximal tubular citrate reabsorption during systemic metabolic acidosis.

right.title: Clinical Consequences
points: Recurrent colic: Nephrolithiasis requiring urological stenting
Bone disease: Progressive osteomalacia and rickets

steps.tx: **Proximal renal tubular acidosis**, designated as **Type 2 RTA**, arises from defective proximal tubule bicarbonate reabsorption, linked to basolateral **NBCe1** sodium-bicarbonate cotransporter dysfunction. It manifests with a **fractional excretion of bicarbonate** exceeding **15%** during intravenous bicarbonate loading, confirming profound impairment of upstream proximal reclamation.

steps.tx: **Type 2 RTA** commonly presents as an integral component of generalized **Fanconi syndrome** in affected individuals. Detailed laboratory findings demonstrate renal **glucosuria** in the presence of completely normal blood glucose concentrations, generalized **aminoaciduria**, marked hyperuricosuria, and hypophosphatemic rickets or osteomalacia from persistent renal phosphate wasting.

steps.tx: **Type 4 RTA** represents hyperkalemic distal RTA caused by aldosterone deficiency or collecting duct **aldosterone resistance**, termed **hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism**. It is characterized by hyperkalemia, normal anion gap acidosis, and intact urine acidification with urine pH below **5.5**, commonly seen in diabetic nephropathy.

steps.tx: Calculating the **urine osmolal gap** estimates **urinary ammonium** excretion: measured osmolality minus **2** times sodium plus potassium, plus urea divided by **2.8**, plus glucose divided by **18**. A value under **40** mOsm/kg confirms defective **distal acidification** in normal anion gap acidosis.
steps.say: Calculating the urine osmolal gap estimates urinary ammonium excretion: measured osmolality minus two times sodium plus potassium, plus urea divided by two point eight, plus glucose divided by eighteen. A value under forty mOsm/kg confirms defective distal acidification in normal anion gap acidosis.

steps.tx: Autoimmune rheumatologic conditions represent major clinical causes of acquired distal tubular injury. **Sjogren syndrome**, systemic lupus erythematosus, and **autoimmune** thyroiditis are the most frequent secondary etiologies of classical adult distal **Type 1 RTA**, mediated by autoantibodies against intercalated cell transport proteins and chronic lymphocytic interstitial inflammation.

left.title: Sjogren Syndrome RTA
points: Associated feature: Severe sensorineural hearing loss

steps.tx: Mitochondrial nephrotoxins induce acquired proximal tubular damage leading to transport breakdown. **Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate**, **ifosfamide**, and platinum chemotherapeutics cause selective mitochondrial toxicity, presenting clinically with acquired **Fanconi syndrome** and proximal **Type 2 RTA** accompanied by severe hypophosphatemia and progressive renal decline.
